summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding presented after a mechanical fall from bed, which caused him to miss hemodialysis. He reported left arm and leg pain but had no head injury or fracture on imaging. His potassium was elevated at 6.1, rising to 7.3 despite initial medical treatment, necessitating emergency hemodialysis. Post-dialysis, his electrolytes normalized, and his symptoms improved. Evaluation ruled out DVT and acute intracranial or spinal injury. He was managed with pain medication, including a new prescription for acetaminophen, and discharged home with instructions to continue all home medications, monitor for symptoms, and prevent future falls.
